rationale: The worker's recorded plan remains defensible: repair boundary accounting, correct the partially covered-cell initialization comparison, and preserve the physical mapping and full window while testing numerical controls. The completed larger patch provides useful exploratory comparison: window-mean departures differ from the base by approximately 0.0021 for ions and 0.0013 for electrons. This does not establish boundary independence or support the hypothesis. Unaccounted open-domain energy decreases of 17.1% and 11.3%, initial matching discrepancies, sampling uncertainty and numerical-scale qualification remain unresolved. The boundary-accounting pilot failed on an API boundary-name lookup after 6.9 seconds; this is an implementation blocker, not adverse physical evidence. Budget feasibility is favorable for targeted work: the refinement pilot measured about 0.128 seconds per evolution step, implying roughly 470 seconds of evolution to reach 0.8, plus initialization, diagnostics and new accounting overhead. Its intentionally short duration collected useful timing information. Approximately 4,060 seconds remain, but valid scientific completion still depends on qualification. No scientific claim is accepted.
next_action: Repair the boundary-buffer interface using the installed API and repeat one bounded check that exercises actual particle loss, cumulative absorbed energy and field-flux accounting; a successful empty-buffer call alone is insufficient. Verify the corrected initialization comparison against the exact physical bin coverage without adjusting the transferred physics. Then use the measured throughput to run the smallest informative full-window numerical control, with the prepared 576-square refinement a practical candidate. Preserve the source, mapping, measurement region, candidate [0.3,0.8] window and explicit stability constraints. Its pilot already supplies enough startup timing; further early-time polishing needs a specific unresolved question. Use observed estimator noise and control discrepancies to choose the next particle/seed or timestep comparison instead of launching an unrestricted matrix. The base grid has dx/Debye length approximately 3.68; the refinement alone does not establish adequate kinetic resolution. Present that limitation, boundary sensitivity, relaxation evidence, initial matching tolerances, relativistic correction and the proposed uncertainty rule to the separate methods reviewer. Obtain review of the complete prospective measurement contract before decisive runs, and collect fresh evidence under it rather than relabeling these exploratory trajectories. Update cost estimates after accounting overhead is measured and preserve time for independent review.
